description: Reviewed family-level marker support and suppression rules for real-world job-title patterns. These rules are intentionally narrow, role-head gated, and family-scoped.

rules.familyLabel: Electronics and telecommunications installers and repairers
rules.notes: Telecom/network equipment titles should reinforce the electronics and telecommunications installer family even when ESCO leaf aliases are sparse.
Telecom/network equipment titles should not drift toward assembly-only families.

Mechanical assembly and automated-installation titles often use market wording that is broader than ESCO leaf aliases but still points to the assembly branch. Excludes 'mecanic' (repairer/maintenance role head, not assembly -- see ro_machinery_mechanic_agricultural_support).

rules.familyLabel: Electronics and telecommunications installers and repairers
rules.notes: Assembly-heavy titles should not gain telecom-installer family support without network/telecom grounding. Excludes 'mecanic' (repairer/maintenance role head, not assembly).
Assistant-plus-pharmacy titles usually express pharmacy-assistant or pharmacy-technician intent rather than pharmacist intent.
Boutique and retail wording should reinforce shop-salesperson families for market sales-advisor titles.
Customer-service wording should reinforce client-information and contact-centre families.
Customer-service titles should not drift to secretary-oriented families without stronger administrative evidence.
Mechanical agricultural-equipment titles usually express repair and maintenance work rather than assembly.
Heavy-vehicle licence and route markers should reinforce heavy-truck driving families.

rules.familyLabel: Electronics and telecommunications installers and repairers
rules.notes: Electrical-network electrician titles with MT/JT markers should not drift to telecom-installer families from generic network wording alone.
Assembly-operator wording should reinforce assembler families over generic supervisor interpretations.
Product-audit and quality-audit technician titles should reinforce general engineering-technician families rather than unrelated cultural or artistic technician branches.
